title.title: An asymptotic formula for the number of totients
title.subtitle: Claim: an explicit asymptotic for $V(x)$, the number of values of $\varphi$ up to $x$, and $V(cx)/V(x) \to c$

panels.caption: marked: values of Euler's $\varphi$. $V(x)$ counts the marked numbers up to $x$

beats.text: Which numbers are values of $\varphi(n)$? No odd number above 1 is
Ford (1998) found the order of magnitude of $V(x)$, not an asymptotic
The claim: an asymptotic, up to a bounded oscillating factor $C(x)$

achievement.context: Before: the order of magnitude of $V(x)$ (Ford 1998)
achievement.note: $C(x)$ oscillates and is defined as a limit, not a closed-form constant

sources.quote: Gives an explicit asymptotic equivalent V(x) ~ (explicit scale) x C(x) for the number of distinct totient values up to x, with a positive bounded phase-dependent factor
in particular V(cx)/V(x) -> c for every fixed c > 0 (Erdos-Hall regular variation question)
Ford (Annals 1998) determined the order of magnitude
The 'asymptotic formula' has an oscillating (phase-dependent) bounded factor defined by a limit, not a closed-form constant.
